title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache parallelism
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: our monorepo CI has grown slow and brittle — a single monolithic workflow runs lint, unit tests, integration tests and release steps which increases queue pressure and cache contention. This PR splits the monolith into three targeted workflows (lint, test, release) and introduces more deterministic cache keys and parallelism limits to reduce GH Actions queuing and speed up common developer loops.

What changed (high level):
- Split .github/workflows/ci.yml into .github/workflows/lint.yaml, test.yaml, release.yaml. Each workflow now has clearly scoped jobs and smaller matrices.
- Introduced a reusable composite action .github/actions/cache-helper that centralizes cache key generation and restore/save semantics. Cache key now includes repo hash + matrix identifier + node-version to avoid collisions across parallel jobs.
- Reduced excessive matrix parallelism for integration tests and replaced naive parallel: ${{ matrix.node }} with controlled strategy.matrix.include and max-parallel where appropriate.
- Bumped several GH actions to latest stable (actions/setup-node@v4, actions/cache@v4, actions/checkout@v4) and upgraded the Node runtime in CI images to node:20 where compatibility was verified.
- Added an explicit concurrency group per-branch to prevent duplicate release workflows running concurrently.
- Minor repo hygiene: removed deprecated workflow inputs and simplified secret usage for the release job (use GITHUB_TOKEN + a separate RELEASE_KEY only in release workflow).

Checklist:
- [x] Split workflows and validate targeted runs for push/pull_request/schedule events
- [x] Validate cache hit rates improved in internal test runs
- [x] Bump GH Actions versions and smoke-test node20 in CI images
- [x] Confirm release workflow concurrency and gating logic

Testing and rollout notes:
- Ran the new workflows against a representative branch with the repo test-matrix. Initial run surfaced a cache key collision for the integration matrix; addressed by appending matrix.job_id and retrying.
- Integration test matrix had a flaky test that timed out in the first run (infra flake); reran failed job and it passed. All CI checks are green at merge time.
- Release workflow is gated by a manual approval step in the new release.yaml for safety during initial rollout.

Migration guidance for contributors:
- Developers should see faster feedback: lint runs trigger independently and no longer wait for long-running integration tests.
- If you add a new matrix axis, update .github/actions/cache-helper/README.md to include the axis when forming cache keys to avoid collisions.

Notes: this PR intentionally avoids changing build/test code. Future follow-ups will add per-route caching suggestions from the perf team and instrumentation for cache hit metrics in our Console.
commits: Split ci.yml into lint.yaml, test.yaml, release.yaml
Add composite action for cache helper and centralize cache key logic
Limit integration test matrix parallelism and add max-parallel
Add concurrency groups and manual approval to release workflow

release_notes:
- Split CI into separate lint/test/release workflows to improve feedback latency and reduce queue contention.
- Introduced cache-helper composite action with deterministic cache keys to reduce cross-job collisions.
- Bumped core GH Actions (setup-node, cache, checkout) and moved CI images to node:20 where compatible.
- Added concurrency control and manual approval for release workflow during rollout.
